records.quote: Corollary 3.10. Let X1, ..., Xn (X1*, ..., Xn*) be independent random variables with Xi ~ GE(alpha, lambda_i) (Xi* ~ GE(alpha, lambda*_i)), i = 1, ..., n. If 0 < alpha <= 1 (alpha >= 1) and (lambda_1, ..., lambda_n) >=^w (>=_w) (lambda*_1, ..., lambda*_n), then X_{1:n} >=st (<=st) X*_{1:n}.
records.family: Generalized exponential GE(alpha, lambda_i), common shape alpha
records.compared: scale vectors lambda vs lambda* under weak supermajorization

hypotheses.text: q(alpha, x) is decreasing in x for 0 < alpha <= 1 (via Lemma 2.1 for GE)

records.quote: Example 3.11. Let (X1, X2) ((X1*, X2*)) be a vector of independent heterogeneous GE random variables. (i) Set alpha = 2, (lambda_1, lambda_2) = (4, 0.5) and (lambda*_1, lambda*_2) = (2, 3). Obviously (lambda_1, lambda_2) >=^w_exp (lambda*_1, lambda*_2), however X_{1:2} and X*_{1:2} are not ordered in the usual stochastic order as can be seen in Fig. 1.
records.compared: scale pairs (4, 0.5) vs (2, 3) under exponential weak majorization

conclusion.direction: X_{1:2} and X*_{1:2} are not ordered in the usual stochastic order (survival functions cross, Fig. 1); refutes the conjecture that weak majorization upgrades Corollary 3.10 for alpha >= 1

note: Example 3.11(i) is a counterexample: survival functions cross in Fig. 1, so no st order either direction; both passes' records agree in substance.
